program_title: Maîtrise en génie électrique (M.A.Sc. research profile)
notes: ÉTS offers both M.Eng. (course-based, French only per official page) and M.A.Sc. (research-based, taught in French AND English). Official page states the M.A.Sc. research profile 'can be admitted on the basis of sufficient knowledge of English' provided a faculty supervisor agrees to supervise the thesis — i.e. coursework/supervision can proceed in English even though the institution is nominally French-medium. International applicant deadlines are published separately, confirming international admission. Use the M.A.Sc. (research) profile, not the M.Eng., for English-track international applicants. VLSI/microelectronics research groups exist within the department (check specific profs) — tier could rise to A for specific supervisors doing embedded/VLSI research.

program_title: Maîtrise en génie électrique / M.A.Sc. Electrical Engineering
notes: Official Polytechnique admissions page states primary language of instruction is French ('basic knowledge of the language is recommended') but research-based programs (M.A.Sc./PhD) can be conducted in English via supervisor arrangement, similar to ÉTS. Several third-party aggregators (Educations.com, Global Admissions) list the Electrical Engineering master's as English-taught and open to international students, but this is NOT independently confirmed on the official page for coursework — treat as English feasible for the research-based M.A.Sc track only, not guaranteed for M.Eng coursework. International admission is standard (Polytechnique has large international enrollment); official admission requirement: undergraduate engineering degree or equivalent. Flagged as needing direct confirmation with the department before relying on for an English-only applicant.

program_title: Maîtrise en génie électrique (cours) — concentration Microélectronique et bio-ingénierie available
department: Faculté de génie / Département de génie électrique et génie informatique
notes: Official page has a dedicated 'Candidats internationaux réguliers' (regular international candidates) admission section listing requirements (bac+5 engineering degree, 2.7/4.3 average, French proficiency for non-French-educated applicants). Confirms international students are admitted but program is French-medium — French proficiency attestation may be required. Microelectronics and bio-engineering is listed as one of the program's two optional specialization fields. Home to the Interdisciplinary Institute of Technological Innovation (3IT) and the Laboratory of Nanotechnologies and Nanosystems (LN2, joint CNRS unit) — strong VLSI/microelectronics research hub, hence Tier A despite French-medium instruction. Deadline: March 1 for fall-only admission.

program_title: Maîtrise en génie électrique (avec mémoire / M.Sc.)
department: Département de génie électrique et de génie informatique
notes: Official program page explicitly warns teaching is in French ('Courses are offered in French, and assignments/exams are written in that language... a student who does not master the language well enough could struggle'). University has a dedicated International Applicants page (ete.ulaval.ca/en/future-students/international-applicants) confirming international admission with financial aid/scholarship options (e.g. Quebec PBEEE merit scholarship via FRQNT). No English track found — this is a genuine French-only program despite being a major engineering school; include but flag language barrier clearly to the user.

program_title: Maîtrise en génie électrique (profil avec mémoire) — specializations in power distribution networks and photonics/microelectronics
notes: Verified directly via UQO's own official program document (etudier.uqo.ca, program 7543). Admission requires a bachelor's in electrical or computer engineering with minimum 3.0/4.3 average (or equivalent degree in a related field such as project management or mathematics, assessed individually). The program document applies a French-language proficiency requirement to 'all applicants' (not domestic-only), implying international students are admitted subject to meeting UQO's language policy — standard for Quebec public universities, not a domestic-only restriction. Photonics and microelectronics is one of the program's named specializations alongside power distribution networks, supporting Tier A. Instruction is French-medium; no English track found. International tuition (~CAD 24,737/yr per third-party aggregator, unverified on official page).

program_title: Maîtrise en génie électrique (avec mémoire) — program code 3824
notes: Confirmed program exists (École d'ingénierie, code 3824, with-thesis profile). UQTR's international-students admission policy (require foreign bachelor's degree to be recognized as equivalent) applies generally to graduate admission, and a 'Créneaux d'expertise' scholarship specifically for international students entering engineering master's programs (including génie électrique) was documented (as of a 2022 source — value may be outdated, verify currency). Program is French-medium. Contact: dir.cycles.sup.gegi@uqtr.ca.

university: Institut national de la recherche scientifique (INRS)
program_title: Maîtrise en télécommunications (profil avec mémoire) — program code 3404
notes: INRS is a graduate-and-research-only institute (no undergraduate programs); this telecommunications master's (45 credits, 33 for thesis, 2 yrs full-time) is adjacent to EE/ECE (wireless, optical, sensor communications, ultrafast photonics per a third-party listing) and could be Tier B/C depending on specialization. Admission requires a bachelor's in electrical engineering or equivalent. CONFIRMED on INRS's own 'Future International Students' page (inrs.ca/en): states more than 60% of the student body is international, from ~50 countries, and explicitly notes French proficiency is NOT a selection criterion for admission to graduate programs — admitted students instead get two years post-enrollment to reach working French via the International French Test. This is a strong, explicit international-admission confirmation, and notably removes the French-language barrier as an admission gate (unlike UQO/Laval/Sherbrooke).
